name: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc.
summary: AMC announced refinancing of about $1.6 billion of debt due in 2026, moving maturities into 2029 and 2030. The arrangements also provided mechanisms for additional exchanges.

name: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc.
summary: AMC reported completing refinancing arrangements. These included roughly $244 million of new financing primarily intended to refinance 2026 maturities, conversion of $143 million of debt into equity, and settlement of litigation involving holders of its 2029 secured notes.

name: iHeartMedia, Inc.
summary: iHeartMedia reported completion of exchanges involving about $4.8 billion of iHeartCommunications debt. Most maturities were extended by three years and debt was reduced by more than $440 million.

earlier_evidence.summary: iHeartMedia announced exchange offers for iHeartCommunications notes and term loans, launched on November 15. Supporting holders represented about 85.4% of existing debt. At this stage the exchange was proposed, not completed.

name: JetBlue Airways Corporation
summary: JetBlue disclosed that it raised more than $3 billion in financing during 2024 and deferred approximately $3 billion in capital spending. Its fourth-quarter GAAP net loss was $44 million, despite a positive operating margin.

name: Carvana Co.
summary: S&P raised Carvana's rating to B with a positive outlook, citing stronger operating performance and credit metrics. Its senior secured debt rating rose from B-minus to B.

name: Boeing Co.
summary: S&P affirmed Boeing at BBB-minus while retaining negative CreditWatch. A $24.3 billion equity and equity-linked issuance reduced financing pressure, but strike disruption and cash-flow recovery remained concerns.

name: FAT Brands Inc.
summary: FAT Brands disclosed receiving acceleration notices on November 17 covering notes issued by four securitization subsidiaries. The trustee declared principal and accrued interest immediately due.

name: Vroom Inc
summary: Vroom completed its recapitalization and exited Chapter 11. Convertible notes became equity, leaving the parent without long-term debt. Subsidiary UACC retained securitization and trust-preferred obligations.

name: Vertex Energy Inc
summary: Vertex completed restructuring and exited Chapter 11 as a private company. It reduced prepetition debt by about $320 million and secured commitments for up to $100 million of exit financing, including $40 million borrowed at emergence.

earlier_evidence.summary: Vertex announced a restructuring agreement supported by all term lenders and commenced Chapter 11 proceedings. Lenders agreed to provide $80 million of additional debtor-in-possession financing, subject to conditions.
